cold_open.hook: AT&T beat earnings but can't sell it—subscribers up, revenue down, stock ripping anyway because apparently that's how this works now.

markets.macro_note: Dow holding, Nasdaq sliding, energy up on oil jump, mega-cap tech taking it on the chin.

big_story.story_title: AT&T Earnings Beat, Revenue Light As Wireless Subscribers Top Estimates
big_story.angle: AT&T crushed subscriber adds but revenue missed—the disconnect is the story: are investors pricing in future pricing power, or is the market just rewarding growth at any cost?

quick_hits.angle: Jensen Huang goes on offense about Chinese AI while the West panics over Kimi—he's betting the geopolitical risk is overblown and the market's already priced it in.
The Fed sounded the alarm on Anthropic's Mythos model but didn't actually have access to it for months—regulators playing catch-up theater while the AI moves faster.
SMCI surging on Alphabet and Tesla earnings coming—the AI infrastructure play is betting the big boys will keep spending, which is a bet on capex not slowing.
Rubio warns Tehran's Hormuz threat could roil global markets—11 straight nights of U.S. strikes and the oil market's barely flinching, which is either confidence or complacency.

odd_thing.joke_angle: Honda's 2026 Prelude is a hybrid marvel—a car so technologically advanced it's basically a rolling spreadsheet that also has cup holders.

sign_off.callback_target: AT&T's revenue miss that nobody cares about because the subscriber number was too loud
